scenarios: a fail-closed before_tool hook that sleeps past its 300 ms timeout is killed and change.apply is POLICY_DENIED/HOOK_TIMEOUT with the file untouched
a fail-open hook exiting 3 is recorded FAILED and the change happens
a hook answering allow under a policy denying fs.write changes nothing: the kernel's deny stands and the answer is MALFORMED
an observing hook that denies is IGNORED; an after_tool observer receives the typed hooks-1 request with the result
before_run is observed and a before_model interceptor stops the run (HOOK_DENIED) before the provider is asked
a repository's hook is refused until the session trusts the repository
audit: DOCUMENTED-ONLY before: the configuration layers resolved a hooks list that nothing read.
proof: Real Core, real handler processes: typed hooks at lifecycle points with timeouts and fail policies, recorded on the task's log, that can deny but never allow.
negative_proof: Mutation: dropping the hook denial in the pipeline lets the slow hook's call succeed and fails the test.

ci.note: every job green on macOS, Linux and Windows on the rebased head (after IMP-EV-0029 landed); one change carries IMP-EV-0042, 0139 and 0240

limitations: Handlers run as host processes with a scrubbed environment (not sandboxed further, like MCP stdio servers); payloads are summaries; only tool arguments can be rewritten; no signature or marketplace trust on extensions in this change (IMP-EV-0225).
